findings.title: Same bug class still live in src/graphics/shader/**: KYTY_AV_TRACE is now read two different ways, and some switches that change behaviour or cost still turn on by presence
findings.scenario: This is the leftover of the rule that files under src/graphics/shader/** must not change, not a mistake in the ~75 converted sites. I checked all 74 removed getenv lines plus the TRACE_CS and GPU_CHECKPOINTS special cases, and each one keeps the old behaviour for every truthy value. No converted site uses the pointer afterwards except the two where it is guaranteed non-null (strcmp(checkpoints,"nv") and string_view(value)). Where the problem remains: (a) KYTY_AV_TRACE is the only variable that crosses the boundary. With KYTY_AV_TRACE=0, FrameStats::Enabled(), AvTraceEnabled(), videoOut, pthread, audio and libAudio2 now read it as off. But ShaderRecompiler.cpp:595 and :739 still test getenv("KYTY_AV_TRACE") != nullptr. So a run with KYTY_AV_TRACE=0 plus --graphics-debug-dump (or early_dump) still prints 'AvTrace: dump decoded/ir' lines while every other AvTrace line is suppressed. (b) KYTY_SRT_VERIFY=0 (SrtWalker.cpp:2357, a runtime SRT evaluation path, not translation) still runs both SRT evaluators and prints SrtVerify output: the same kind of cost trap as KYTY_GPU_CHECKPOINTS=0. KYTY_BVH_STUB=0 (frontend/translate/Memory.cpp:713) still stubs every ray as a miss. KYTY_SAMPLE_LOD0=0 (spirvEmitterImage.cpp:758) still forces LOD 0 on pixel-shader samples. Both of those also change the translated SPIR-V. The comment in envFlag.h says the presence test 'sat behind every other on/off switch of this class', which reads as if the class is closed; for these files it is not. Outside shader/** no presence-tested on/off switch remains; the only leftover presence test outside shader/**, KYTY_RET_TRACE_AFTER_THREAD, holds a thread name. Fixing this would change the translator source hash, so the fix is a documented exception or warning, not a code edit in this session.

reason: The code facts in the claim are accurate, but none of them is a real defect introduced by the diff. (a) KYTY_AV_TRACE: ShaderRecompiler.cpp:595 and :739 still test presence, but only inside `if (options.dump_ir)`. On the game path dump_ir is set only when the shader log is not silent (pipelineCache.cpp:3471), and the pretranslation job defaults it to false (computePretranslation.h:172). So with KYTY_AV_TRACE=0 the only effect is two timing LOGF lines per shader, and only in a run that already writes full decoded/IR dumps per shader. There is no cost trap: the timer and one log line are nothing next to the dump itself. It is also not a regression: before the diff KYTY_AV_TRACE=0 turned on every AvTrace line, and now it turns on only these dump-only lines. The diff strictly narrows the old wrong behaviour. (b) KYTY_SRT_VERIFY (SrtWalker.cpp:2357), KYTY_BVH_STUB (Memory.cpp:713) and KYTY_SAMPLE_LOD0 (spirvEmitterImage.cpp:758) are untouched lines that predate the diff. They sit in files globbed into the translator source hash (CMakeLists.txt:204-222). The session's sealed plan (docs/session-102/pred/01_m5_bench.md:39,135) requires the translator hash to stay 2db9065a, so leaving them out was deliberate, and the reviewer admits this. They are debug aids documented as "=1" switches. What remains is the wording of the envFlag.h comment ("sat behind every other on/off switch of this class"), which is a documentation nit, not a runtime defect.

I checked the source, and the claim does not describe a real defect introduced by the session-102 diff.

1. **No file under src/graphics/shader/ is modified.** `git status -- src/` lists none, so every presence test there is unchanged from before the session:
   - SrtWalker.cpp:2357 (`KYTY_SRT_VERIFY`)
   - Memory.cpp:713 (`KYTY_BVH_STUB`)
   - spirvEmitterImage.cpp:758 (`KYTY_SAMPLE_LOD0`)
   - ShaderRecompiler.cpp:595 and :739 (`KYTY_AV_TRACE`)

   Leaving them out was deliberate. CMakeLists.txt:206-222 globs `graphics/shader/recompiler/**` into the translator source set. Editing those files changes the translation-cache signature, as CLAUDE.md records for sessions 58-59, and forces a cold shader and pipeline cache. The claim itself says the fix would be a documented exception, not a code edit. That makes it a scope note, not a bug.

2. **The only effect the diff creates across that boundary is harmless.** It applies when `KYTY_AV_TRACE=0` is set and `dump_ir` is on (`--graphics-debug-dump` / `early_dump`). In that case the two `if (av_trace)` blocks at ShaderRecompiler.cpp:595-602 and :739-746 still print one timing line each ("AvTrace: dump decoded" / "AvTrace: dump ir") per shader.
   - They only log a timing number for a dump that `dump_ir` already performs.
   - They change no behaviour, no SPIR-V, no cost that matters, and no measurement.
   - Before the diff, `KYTY_AV_TRACE=0` turned on every AvTrace site and also `FrameStats::Enabled()`. The diff therefore makes things strictly better, not worse.

3. **The envFlag.h comment is not a behaviour defect.** "the same test sat behind every other on/off switch of this class" is a past-tense account of the session-101 finding. At most it is a documentation nit.

No wrong behaviour is attributable to the diff.
